sections.html:
Tooele County fills a big stretch of northwestern Utah west of Salt Lake County, covering 7,286 square miles, of which 6,941 are land. Most residents live in a strip along the eastern edge, in towns such as Tooele (35,742 people in 2020), Grantsville (12,617) and the unincorporated community of Stansbury Park (9,851). Wendover, on the Nevada line, had 1,115. The county's population was 72,698 in 2020, up from 40,735 in 2000, so it has nearly doubled in two decades.

Two houses with the same county mailing address can sit in very different settings, from a town lot in Tooele to acreage at the edge of the desert, and the assessor values them separately.

Stansbury Park deserves a note if you own there. It began in 1970 as a planned community with a golf course and a man-made lake. Water and sewer come from the Stansbury Park Improvement District, and the Stansbury Park Community Association gives preliminary approval to housing and remodeling plans. Buyers there ask about association rules early.

The county values property as of January 1 and treats November 30 as the last day to pay without penalty.

WhenWhat happens
January 1Property is valued as it stood on this date
May 22Assessor completes the roll and certifies values to the Auditor
May or JuneTax sale for parcels more than five years delinquent
July or AugustValuation notices mailed
August or SeptemberBoard of Equalization window, 45 days from mailing
By November 1Property tax notices mailed
November 30Last day to pay without penalty
December 1Unpaid taxes become delinquent

The assessor dates page posts the current schedule. The Treasurer's office at 47 S. Main Street in Tooele answers questions at (435) 843-3190, Monday through Friday, 8:00 am to 5:00 pm.

sections.h2: Winters and wear on a house
sections.html:
Summers are hot and dry and winters are cold, with real snow. Normal highs are 38.7 degrees in January and 91.4 in July. Tooele gets about 18.44 inches of precipitation and 75.3 inches of snowfall a year, with a record high of 106 degrees and a record low of minus 16. Wendover is far drier, at about 4.58 inches a year.

A buyer's inspector will look first at the roof, the furnace and the water heater, then at settling and grading around the foundation. A house that sat vacant through a few winters shows more of that wear. Selling as-is means you skip those repairs.

You have 45 days from the mailing of your Notice of Property Valuation, or until September 15, to file with the county Board of Equalization.

At least one of four kinds of evidence is required:

  • Recent comparable sales of similar homes that closed before January 1 for less than the assessed value.
  • A closing statement from a purchase made before January 1, with a bank-required appraisal for short sales, bank-owned sales and foreclosures.
  • An appraisal with an effective date within the year.
  • A written statement of a factual error, such as wrong square footage or a carport listed as a garage.

High taxes by themselves are not grounds, because rates come from the cities, school districts and other districts that hold public hearings on their budgets. If the board's answer disappoints you, the State Tax Commission takes a written appeal within 30 days of the board's decision, filed through the county auditor. A typical homeowner saves $4 to $8 in tax for each $1,000 of value removed. The Tax Commission's appeals publication explains the steps.

sections.h2: The primary residential exemption and a sale
sections.html:
A qualifying primary home is taxed on 55 percent of its market value, and the exemption does not pass to a new owner automatically.

The exemption covers up to one acre per residential unit, requires use as a primary residence, and counts part-year use of at least 183 consecutive days. Each household gets one. When a property changes hands, the new owner has to apply on Form TC-473A, emailed to assessorsurvey@tooeleco.gov. If the form does not come back within 30 days, the county sends a notice with 30 more days, and after that the exemption is removed.

Starting January 1, 2027, any change in ownership interest, including a deed or trust transfer, calls for a new form under 2026 SB 238, and applications are due to the Board of Equalization by September 15. A lost exemption means taxation at 100 percent of market value. Heirs and landlords selling a Tooele County rental should know this before they list.

Unpaid taxes become delinquent on December 1, penalties and interest begin to build, and a parcel can go to a tax sale once it is more than five years behind. Penalties have been the greater of 1 percent or $10 at first, rising to the greater of 2.5 percent or $10 after January 31, with interest of 10 percent on the December 1 balance. Call the Treasurer for the current figures.

The Auditor's tax sale is advertised weekly for four weeks, and owners can redeem before the sale. If you are behind on taxes and want out, call us before the delinquency list is published. We ask the Treasurer for the payoff and plan the closing around it.

Back taxes do not stop a sale, but they change the order of things. The county's lien comes ahead of most others, so the balance has to be paid at closing, usually out of your proceeds. Start by asking the Treasurer for a payoff good through your expected closing date. If more than one year is open, expect the title company to want all of it cleared.

Gather your deed, your most recent tax notice and the valuation notice. If the house is a rental or has been vacant, check that notices were going to the right mailing address, since a missed notice is a common reason taxes fall behind. A cash buyer can work around the problem: we get a current balance from the Treasurer and handle it through closing, for a house in any Tooele County town from Tooele and Grantsville to Stansbury Park.

sections.h2: What to have ready for the Treasurer's office
sections.html: A short list saves a second trip. Bring the parcel number, a photo ID and the name exactly as it appears on the deed. The office is at 47 S. Main Street, Tooele, UT 84074, and the phone number is (435) 843-3190. For questions about value, the primary residence form or the appeal, the assessor's office handles those instead, so ask which office you need before you drive over.

faqs.q: When are Tooele County property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 30 is the last day to pay current-year real property tax without penalty. Taxes become delinquent on December 1, and notices are mailed by November 1.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Tooele County property valuation?
faqs.a: The later of September 15 or 45 days after the valuation notice was mailed. File with the county Board of Equalization and bring comparable sales, an appraisal, a closing statement or proof of a factual error.

faqs.q: Do I lose the 45 percent residential exemption when I sell?
faqs.a: The seller stops qualifying once the home is sold, and the new owner must apply separately. Without an approved application the property can be taxed at 100 percent of market value.

faqs.q: Where is the Tooele County Treasurer?
faqs.a: At 47 S. Main Street, Tooele, UT 84074, phone (435) 843-3190. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 am to 5:00 pm.

faqs.q: Can you buy a Tooele County house with back taxes owed?
faqs.a: Yes. We get a current balance from the Treasurer and handle it through closing. A house in any Tooele County town qualifies, from Tooele and Grantsville to Stansbury Park.
